sections.title: Executive Summary
paragraphs: The aim of this document is to describe the web service JI Receipt in terms of "what is it" and "how to use it". It describes the webservice data-model, supported operation and related behavior and available interfaces.
Before going deeper with specific features of this webservice please ensure to review the document “JINT WS Development_Kit - Web Services Overview” which applies to all webservices
The structure of the current document is the following:
1. Import:
2. Request data format [Import]: describes the structure of the import request.
3. Behavior [Import]: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of particular processes
4. Response data format [Import]: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes
5. Export:
6. Component filters [Export]: describes which sections of a receipt can be exported. The use of a component filter increments the number of sections in the response to every receipt exported.

7. Condition filters [Export]: describes which fields can be used to filter the receipt to be extracted on specific conditions. So, the use of a condition filter allows to decrease the number of receipts extracted.
8. Export data format [Export]: describes the structure of the response in terms of exported fields and sections.
9. Error codes [Export]: contains a list of possible error codes
10. Validate:

11. Request data format [Validate]: describes the structure of the validation request. The request is composed of sections and every section is composed of fields to be filled. This paragraph specifies which fields are mandatory and those that can be omitted.
12. Behavior [Validate]: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of some particular processes
13. Response data format [Validate JIInvoice method]: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes
14. SOAP INTERFACE
15. Available methods: contains the list of the methods provided by the web service.
16. WSDL: in this paragraph is attached the JIReceipt.wsdl from which the web service has been created and is to be used to generate the client.
17. Endpoints: available webservice SOAP endpoint URLs
18. Request samples: sample SOAP requests to invoke the webservice
19. REST INTERFACE
20. Operation and Endpoints: describes REST available collections. Allowed calls with allowed parameters and supported HTTP methods
21. Request Samples: provides some call examples and a POSTMAN collection with an extensive list of runnable calls

22. Data Types and UI Default Labels: describes the type of the fields and the corresponding label in English language in the platform with the aim to simplify the mapping between the fields visible in the platform and the fields used in the web service.

sections.title: Export
paragraphs: Receipt export method retrieves a list of information about JI Receipt matching optional filtering criteria.
This main Receipt setting information can be further enriched by specifically requesting additional information.
The list of returned receipts matching requested filter is always ordered by internal (JI) identifier in ascending order.

Export JI Receipt Web Service method is paged. It needs a field “startAt” representing the index of the first record to be returned (according to last update date order). If not expressed or a not positive value is passed, the value 1 is assumed.

sections.title: Condition filters [Export]
paragraphs: Here are defined extraction condition filters, i.e. the rule to be used for data filtering.
A same condition filter can be expressed more than once. All specified filters are requested to be matched (they are all applied in AND clause).
For instance, it is possible to apply the following filters:
The result will be that all receipt having creation date greater than 2011-11-20 AND lower than 2012-01-20 (between 2011-11-20 AND 2012-01-20) will be retrieved.
Condition filters are also available server side as restrictive conditions. The filter conditions entered client side will be joined with the filter conditions configured server side.

It is possible to enable the component filters according to particular values of the condition filters server side. By this way, it is possible to configure different chains, everyone with different restrictive conditions and therefore with different subsets of component filters enabled.

For instance, based on the specific configuration set up for the single integration, will be possible to allow the webservice client to export only receipt having source equal to “manual”, even if this filter is not set by the integration client.

rows: Date and time receipt information was last updated

Date filtering accepts following operators:
EQUAL: object last update date must be equal to provided value
NOTEQUAL: any object whose last update date is different from provided value
GREATER_THAN: any object whose last update date is equal or greater than provided value
LESS_THAN: any object whose last update date is lower or than provided value
Date value must be expressed in the form
yyyy-MM-dd
or
yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS Z
eg. 2012-03-01 or 2012-03-01 12:36:42.535 +0100

Internal identifier filter accepts following operators:
EQUAL: required field must be equal to provided value
NOTEQUAL: required field must be different from provided value
IN: required field must be present in provided value list
NOT_IN: required field must not be present in provided value list

These filters accept following operators:
EQUAL: required field must match exactly provided value (case sensitive)
NOTEQUAL: required field must be different from provided value
STARTWITH: required field must start with provided value (case insensitive)
CONTAINS: required field must contain provided value (case insensitive)
ENDWITH: required field must terminate with provided value (case insensitive)
Except of “receiptName”, all filters accept also:
IN: required field must be present in provided value list
NOT_IN: required field must not be present in provided value list
The “receiptSource”, “trackingNumber” and “packingSlipNumber” filters accept also the following:
ISNULL: required field is checked to be not valorized
NOTNULL: required field is required to be valorized, no matter value

sections.title: Validate
paragraphs: JI Receipt validate method allows to accept messages from a customer’s ERP system to validate a purchase receipt by entirely accepting or discarding it, or by signaling that some receipt line elements failed the validation while at least one of them succeeded.

sections.title: Request data format [Validate]
paragraphs: Following table shows the structure of the validate request to submit.

rows: Unique identifier for the receipt export message which with this receipt was saved

Object defining receipt validation result.
See section “ValidateReceiptData [Validate]” below

Status of the validation request.
It can assume following value:
Approved: all receipt elements passed validation
Rejected: all receipt elements failed validation
Returned: one or more receipt elements failed the validation, but at least one element or field succeeded
New value of the receipt Number to be used, in substitution of current one.
Note to provide additional information about the object and its status.

sections.title: Behavior [Validate]
paragraphs: When “validate” JIReceipt method is called, system update the validation status that is shown by means of the “export” JIReceipt method (see field “validationStatus” in chapter above).
To correctly manage such information, it is necessary to know the internal identifier of the receipt.

sections.title: Response data format [Validate]
paragraphs: Receipt Validate response is made of following fields

rows:
Global operation result.
See section “Error codes [Validate]” below

Operation result description.
See section “ValidateResponseMessage [Validate]” below
Receipt validation message identifier provided in request

Response timestamp in the format
yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ

Validation response result.
See section “ValidateStatus [Validate]” below

Container of validation error information
See section “ValidateError [Validate]” below

Validation response result code.
200 - The request was processed successfully.
400 - The request could not be understood due to syntax errors.
500 - The request could not be processed due to a transient error.
Type of error: Error or Warning
Operation was not completed due to error in provided data.
Invalid SOAP Request Object (SOAP Request doesn’t match web service definition or request contains information that are not compliant with instance configuration or user permission)
Unauthorized Method (Web Service method isn’t configured to be executed)
Unable to acquire lock (Web Service is configured to serialize different call coming from a same client and it hasn’t been able to acquire lock to satisfy request for configured timeout)
